name: Making Do

angles.text: As an Alliance traveler, you see how distance and Stormwind's strained treasury leave Auberdine without financial support.
As a night elf, you see that neither your human allies across the sea nor Darnassus nearby is helping Auberdine with its local struggles.
As a human, you see how Stormwind's depleted coffers and hardship across its lands prevent the kingdom from funding aid overseas.

faq.answer: Making Do sends a traveler across the sea with Baros Alexston's reply from Stormwind to Elder Thundris Windweaver in Auberdine. The letter says Stormwind cannot afford to send aid to Darkshore.
faq.q: What is the quest Making Do?

faq.answer: Stormwind's coffers are badly depleted, and its remaining resources are stretched thin across its own lands. The kingdom cannot afford to help Auberdine.
faq.q: Why does Stormwind refuse to aid Auberdine?

faq.answer: Thundris Windweaver receives the letter with sadness and accepts that Auberdine must rely on itself. Neither Stormwind nor Darnassus is providing support.
faq.q: How does Thundris Windweaver react to the news?

faq.answer: Baros Alexston sent the reply from Stormwind. He expresses sympathy for Auberdine while explaining that the kingdom cannot afford to help.
Thundris Windweaver says neither Stormwind nor Darnassus has helped Auberdine. The settlement must rely on itself.
Alexston's Reply is delivered to Thundris Windweaver in the port town of Auberdine, on the coast of Darkshore.

sections.body: A traveler carries Alexston's Reply across the sea to Elder Thundris Windweaver in Auberdine. The letter offers no relief or troops. Stormwind's representative explains that the kingdom's treasury is running low, and the little wealth left is stretched thin across its own struggling territories.
sections.title: A Courier Across the Sea

sections.body: Thundris Windweaver receives the reply with regret and thanks the traveler for the long journey. Stormwind cannot help, and Darnassus has offered no aid either. Thundris accepts that Auberdine and its people must rely on themselves, with their fate resting in their own hands.
sections.title: Left to Their Own Fate

summary: Auberdine waits for word from Stormwind, and the answer brings no aid. Making Do sends Alexston's Reply across the sea to Elder Thundris Windweaver, carrying a refusal from a kingdom whose coffers are nearly empty.
